security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL retains the MT_ASYNC bit (bit 36 in xenvcfg; former bit adjacent to MT_MODE in mseccfg) as a writable control register field after the spec removes it, causing writes to a now-WPRI bit to configure non-existent asynchronous tag-check behavior, or the store tag-check FSM still conditionally defers software check exceptions based on this stale control bit instead of always reporting synchronously
security_spec.summary: Stale MT_ASYNC CSR bit left in hardware after spec removal: writes to now-WPRI bit can enable undocumented asynchronous exception deferral, breaking synchronous trap-delivery guarantees and opening a window where tag-mismatched stores retire without immediate exception

findings.finding: EnvCfg base class contains no MT_ASYNC or any MTE-related field. Bit positions 63,62,61,59,33:32,7,6,5:4,3,2,0 are used for STCE/PBMTE/ADUE/DTE/PMM/CBZE/CBCFE/CBIE/SSE/LPE/FIOM respectively. Bit 36 is not defined, meaning writes are implicitly RO-zero (WPRI), which is correct behavior per spec.
mseccfg CSR defines only PMM(33:32), MLPE(10), SSEED(9), USEED(8), RLB(2), MMWP(1), MML(0). No MT_MODE or adjacent MT_ASYNC field exists. No writable control for async MTE behavior exists.
Store pipeline contains no MTE tag-check logic, no async tag mismatch FSM, and no deferred software-check exception handling. Tag checking is absent entirely, consistent with no MTE support.
findings.snippet: (no MTE-related code found in store pipeline)

findings.finding: TLB contains no MTE tag-check integration. No tag memory lookups or MTE-related PTE bit handling exists. Since MTE is not implemented, no stale async-mode dependency can exist.
Store buffer contains no deferred tag exception logic or async mode gating. No MTE-related signals or state machines exist.

findings.finding: Store queue contains no MTE tag-check bypass or async tag mismatch state. No MTE-related fields, signals, or control paths exist.
